headline: High-risk filesystem and browser-mediated interaction: Goose can write/egress while pdf.js can render attacker-controlled PDFs, creating injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the user filesystem and use MCP, while pdf.js processes PDF files and runs in a browser-based worker model. If Goose ingests pdf.js-rendered or extracted PDF content from a shared workspace, attacker-controlled document text can be treated as instructions. The pair has a plausible shared-file bridge, so this is not blocked by default.
conditions: IF Goose reads PDF-derived text from the shared workspace without provenance checks
IF pdf.js is used on attacker-supplied PDFs that contain instruction-like text
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Require manual review of PDF-derived text before Goose consumes it
Disable MCP access for untrusted document workflows
Use a provenance tag or filename convention for extracted text
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd and has broad network egress, while pdf.js handles PDF documents and files. If both share a workspace, sensitive code or document contents can flow from Goose into outputs or networked services, and pdf.js can expose document contents to the same workspace. The leakage path exists in default-style shared-file setups.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same cwd or mounted workspace
IF Goose forwards file contents to configured model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per agent
Restrict Goose network egress for sensitive runs
Keep PDFs and source code in different mounts
Redact secrets before either agent processes shared files
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls at the filesystem layer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shell access; pdf.js can run in a browser and read PDF files. In a shared workspace, Goose can mutate files while pdf.js reads them, and Goose can also alter git state without any locking shown. The overlap on the same mutable files makes concurrent corruption or conflicting edits likely.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or directory
IF Goose modifies files while pdf.js is reading or generating PDFs from that directory
mitigations: Run the agents on separate copies of the workspace
Pause one agent before the other writes
Avoid shared git branches during parallel runs
Use file locks for any shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can produce code or file edits, and pdf.js can render or process PDFs that may be treated as authoritative artifacts. If pdf.js consumes Goose-generated documents without verification, errors or fabricated content can cascade into downstream document processing. The pair lacks any documented verification boundary, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF pdf.js is fed documents generated or edited by Goose
IF downstream users treat pdf.js output as authoritative without manual verification
mitigations: Add a human review step before PDF publication
Compare generated PDFs against source files
Mark Goose-produced artifacts as draft
Use checksum checks on intermediate files
requires-engineering: implement validation of document provenance

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles source code and files in cwd and may send content to configured model providers, while pdf.js processes PDF documents locally with no network egress. The main compliance issue is a workspace-policy mismatch rather than a residency breach. Because pdf.js is local-only and no PHI/EU-PII handling is shown, the risk stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared workspace
IF Goose is configured to send that data to external model providers
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Disable external model providers for sensitive runs
Use local-only inputs for pdf.js
Document retention rules for generated artifacts
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies across tools
